drugs.name: Insulin Glargine (Lantus/Basaglar/Semglee)
drugs.mechanism: Long-acting basal insulin analog with amino acid substitutions (A21 Gly→Asn, B31-32 Arg-Arg) that shift the isoelectric point to pH 6.7, forming microprecipitates at subcutaneous pH for slow, peakless 24-hour absorption
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2000. Gold-standard basal insulin for T1D.
drugs.efficacy: Maintains near-physiologic basal insulin levels; reduces HbA1c by 1.5-2.0% when combined with prandial insulin. Reduces severe hypoglycemia vs NPH.

drugs.name: Insulin Lispro (Humalog/Admelog)
drugs.mechanism: Rapid-acting insulin analog with B28 Pro→Lys and B29 Lys→Pro inversion mimicking the natural insulin monomer; rapid dissociation to monomers enables faster absorption and shorter duration of action
drugs.approval: FDA approved 1996. First rapid-acting insulin analog.
drugs.route: Subcutaneous injection or insulin pump (CSII), before meals
drugs.efficacy: Reduces postprandial glucose excursions by 30-40%; onset 15-30 min, peak 1-2 h, duration 3-5 h. Lower postprandial hypoglycemia vs regular insulin.

drugs.name: Insulin Aspart (NovoLog/Fiasp)
drugs.mechanism: Rapid-acting insulin analog with B28 Pro→Asp substitution, reducing hexamer stability and enhancing monomer formation for rapid absorption. Fiasp formulation adds niacinamide and L-arginine for ultra-fast absorption.
drugs.route: Subcutaneous injection or insulin pump, before meals
drugs.efficacy: Onset 10-20 min, peak 1-2 h, duration 3-5 h. Fiasp provides 2x faster initial absorption; superior 1h postprandial glucose vs conventional aspart.

drugs.name: Insulin Degludec (Tresiba)
drugs.mechanism: Ultra-long-acting basal insulin with deletion of B30 Thr and a 16-carbon fatty diacid attached to B29 Lys via glutamic acid spacer; forms stable multi-hexamers in subcutaneous depot for flat, ultra-long >42-hour duration with 4x less variability than glargine
drugs.efficacy: HbA1c reduction 1.5-2.0%; 40% lower rate of nocturnal hypoglycemia vs glargine U100 in T1D (SWITCH 1 trial).

drugs.name: Teplizumab (Tzield)
drugs.mechanism: Humanized FcR-nonbinding anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody that modulates the TCR/CD3 complex, inducing partial CD3 phosphorylation and anergy in effector T cells while expanding CD8+FOXP3+ regulatory T cells, preserving residual β cell function
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2022. First disease-modifying therapy for T1D; delays onset of Stage 3 T1D by median 2-3 years in Stage 2 (autoantibody-positive, dysglycemic) individuals.
drugs.efficacy: Delayed clinical T1D onset by median 2 years vs placebo in TN-10 trial (HR 0.41). Preserved C-peptide levels by ~75% at 2 years in new-onset T1D (AbATE, Protégé trials).

drugs.name: Otelixizumab (ChAglyCD3)
drugs.mechanism: Chimeric/humanized aglycosyl anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody with reduced FcR binding; modulates autoreactive T cell activity through TCR downregulation and induction of T cell tolerance with lower cytokine release than teplizumab
drugs.approval: Investigational. Phase 3 DEFEND-1/2 trials completed but did not meet primary endpoint at the tested dose; lower doses being re-evaluated.
drugs.efficacy: Initial Phase 2 (3.1 mg total dose) preserved β cell function for 18-24 months. Phase 3 DEFEND trials at lower dose (0.45 mg) did not show significant C-peptide preservation, suggesting a dose-response relationship.

drugs.name: Golimumab (Simponi)
drugs.mechanism: Fully human anti-TNF monoclonal antibody neutralizing both soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha, blocking TNFR1/TNFR2 signaling and reducing β cell-destructive inflammation
drugs.approval: Investigational for T1D. Phase 2 T1GER trial showed C-peptide preservation. FDA approved for RA/PsA/AS/UC but not yet for T1D.
drugs.efficacy: In the T1GER Phase 2 trial, golimumab preserved endogenous insulin production (36% higher C-peptide at 52 weeks vs placebo) and reduced exogenous insulin requirements in children/young adults with new-onset T1D.

drugs.name: Abatacept (Orencia)
drugs.mechanism: CTLA4-Ig fusion protein that binds CD80/CD86 on antigen-presenting cells, blocking CD28-mediated T cell costimulation and reducing islet-reactive T cell activation and expansion
drugs.approval: Investigational for T1D. Phase 2 trial showed 9.6-month delay in C-peptide decline. FDA approved for RA but not T1D.
drugs.route: IV infusion monthly or subcutaneous weekly
drugs.efficacy: Slowed decline in C-peptide by 9.6 months in new-onset T1D (TrialNet). At 2 years, C-peptide 59% higher vs placebo. Effect waned after treatment cessation, suggesting continuous therapy is needed.
drugs.category: Investigational Biologic - T Cell Costimulation Blocker

drugs.name: Rituximab (Rituxan)
drugs.mechanism: Chimeric anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody depleting B cells via ADCC, CDC, and apoptosis; removes B cells involved in autoantigen presentation to islet-reactive T cells
drugs.approval: Investigational for T1D. Phase 2 TrialNet study showed transient C-peptide preservation. FDA approved for RA/NHL but not T1D.
drugs.efficacy: In TrialNet Phase 2, rituximab preserved C-peptide at 1 year (20% higher vs placebo) and reduced HbA1c in new-onset T1D. Benefit was most pronounced in younger patients. Effect diminished after B cell repopulation.

drugs.name: Alefacept (Amevive)
drugs.mechanism: LFA-3-Ig (CD58-Ig) fusion protein binding CD2 on effector memory T cells, blocking CD2-CD58 costimulation and selectively depleting pathogenic CD4+CD45RO+ and CD8+ memory T cells via NK cell-mediated ADCC
drugs.approval: Investigational for T1D. T1DAL Phase 2 trial demonstrated C-peptide preservation. Previously FDA approved for psoriasis (withdrawn 2011).
drugs.efficacy: In the T1DAL trial, alefacept preserved C-peptide secretion at 1 year (0.015 vs -0.076 nmol/L placebo) and reduced insulin requirements by 0.09 U/kg/day vs placebo in new-onset T1D. Reduced CD4+ and CD8+ central memory T cells.
drugs.category: Investigational Biologic - Effector Memory T Cell Depletion

drugs.name: Anti-Thymocyte Globulin (ATG/Thymoglobulin)
drugs.target: T Cell Surface Antigens (CD2, CD3, CD4, CD8, CD25, CD44, CD45, etc.)
drugs.mechanism: Rabbit-derived polyclonal IgG targeting multiple T cell surface proteins, depleting effector T cells via complement-mediated lysis and ADCC; at low doses, may preferentially deplete effector cells while sparing Tregs
drugs.approval: Investigational for T1D. Phase 2 START and TrialNet ATG-GCSF trials showed mixed results. Low-dose ATG + G-CSF combination showed promise.
drugs.efficacy: Low-dose ATG (2.5 mg/kg) alone showed transient C-peptide benefit in START trial but did not meet primary endpoint. Low-dose ATG + G-CSF combination significantly preserved C-peptide at 1 year vs placebo in TrialNet study, suggesting synergistic Treg-boosting effect.

drugs.name: Low-Dose Interleukin-2 (Aldesleukin/Proleukin - low dose)
drugs.mechanism: Low-dose recombinant IL-2 selectively expands and activates CD25-high FOXP3+ regulatory T cells (Tregs) over effector T cells due to the higher IL-2R affinity of Tregs, restoring the Treg/Teff balance in islet autoimmunity
drugs.approval: Investigational for T1D. Phase 1/2 trials (DF-IL2, IL-2idea) demonstrated Treg expansion and safety. Phase 2b trials ongoing.
drugs.route: Subcutaneous injection, daily for 5 days every 2-4 weeks
drugs.efficacy: Phase 1/2 trials showed dose-dependent 2-4 fold expansion of peripheral Tregs with minimal Teff activation; preserved C-peptide in a subset of recent-onset T1D patients. No severe hypoglycemia or cytokine release syndrome at low doses.

drugs.name: Verapamil (Calan/Isoptin)
drugs.mechanism: L-type calcium channel blocker that paradoxically reduces β cell TXNIP (thioredoxin-interacting protein) expression. TXNIP is a key inducer of β cell apoptosis via NLRP3 inflammasome activation and is induced by hyperglycemia. Verapamil reduces TXNIP-mediated β cell ER stress and death.
drugs.approval: Investigational for T1D. Phase 2 CLVer trial showed C-peptide preservation. FDA approved for hypertension/arrhythmia but not yet for T1D.
drugs.efficacy: In the CLVer Phase 2 trial, verapamil preserved stimulated C-peptide at 52 weeks (30% higher vs placebo) in children/adolescents with new-onset T1D. Reduced hybrid closed-loop insulin requirements. Well-tolerated.
drugs.category: Investigational Small Molecule - β Cell Preservation

drugs.name: GAD-Alum (Diamyd)
drugs.mechanism: Recombinant human GAD65 protein formulated with alum adjuvant; administered subcutaneously to induce GAD65-specific immune tolerance via induction of GAD65-specific Tregs, Th2 deviation, and suppression of autoreactive Th1 responses against the major β cell autoantigen
drugs.approval: Investigational. Phase 3 DIAGNODE-3 trial ongoing. Prior Phase 3 European trial missed primary endpoint but showed benefit in prespecified subgroups (HLA-DR3-DQ2 positive patients).
drugs.efficacy: In Phase 2b DIAGNODE trial, intralymphatic GAD-alum preserved C-peptide by 58% at 15 months vs placebo in patients carrying HLA-DR3-DQ2. Subgroup analysis of prior Phase 3 European trial showed significant C-peptide preservation in patients diagnosed within 6 months.

drugs.name: Ustekinumab (Stelara)
drugs.target: IL-12/IL-23 (p40 subunit shared by IL12B and IL23A)
drugs.mechanism: Fully human monoclonal antibody targeting the shared p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23, blocking Th1 (IL-12/IFN-γ) and Th17 (IL-23/IL-17) differentiation pathways implicated in islet autoimmunity
drugs.approval: Investigational for T1D. Phase 2 UST1D trial ongoing. FDA approved for psoriasis, PsA, Crohn's, UC but not T1D.
drugs.efficacy: Phase 1b/2 pilot data showed ustekinumab preserved C-peptide in new-onset T1D at 12 months. Reduces IL-17A and IFN-γ production by islet-reactive T cells ex vivo. Phase 2 results pending.
